author: John Connolly, Deputy Commissioner and Minnesota Medicaid Director
title: Corrective Action Plan for Program Integrity Update (revised, to CMS)
notes: Redacted version, released by DHS itself via its program-integrity factcheck page. Addressed to the same CMS officials (Brandt, Brillman) as the December 31 original CAP (src-mn-dhs-2025-12-31-cap-original).
supports: DHS states this revised CAP is submitted 'in response to the letter from Administrator Oz dated January 6, 2026.' This resolves, from a primary Minnesota-agency source, the exact date and signatory of the CMS deficiency letter that research/harvest/oversight-law/GAPS.md item 2 previously listed with an uncertain date (referenced there as a '6 January 2026 letter to Gov. Walz' reproduced only in a third-party circulation, CMS-FILE_6607).
DHS states it 'hosted in-person meetings with CMS staff on January 21 and 22' 2026 as part of finalizing the corrective action plan -- a previously undocumented pair of dated meetings.

This CAP is submitted 'on behalf of Governor Tim Walz' and identifies itself as a 'revised, comprehensive corrective action plan' proposing 'additional program integrity actions' with implementation timeframes and performance metrics.

The letter repeats the same background narrative as the December 31, 2025 original CAP (EO 25-10 on September 17, 2025; the October 2024 EIDBI on-site audit process; the high-risk EIDBI/HSS designation), indicating continuity between the two submissions rather than a materially different factual predicate.
does_not_support: The full text of CMS Administrator Oz's January 6, 2026 deficiency letter itself; only DHS's characterization and response to it.

The March 19, 2026 CMS approval letter (reported in contemporaneous journalism as signed by Kim Brandt) or its content; that document postdates this filing and was not located as a directly retrievable primary PDF in this pass.

The specific 17 corrective-action elements journalism describes (e.g., pausing new providers in 13 high-risk service categories, revalidating 5,500+ providers); this source record captures the letter's framing only, not a itemized element-by-element extraction of the full 20-page attachment in this pass.
